title: Have and have not
description: Say what you have and do not have: relatives, things, time, money and ailments.

guide.title: There is no verb 'to have'
guide.text:
Kannada says 'to me there is ...' or 'near me there is ...'. The verb is iru (ide, iddaane, iddaale, iddaare, ive), and it agrees with the thing possessed, not with the owner.

Pattern 1 - dative + iru. Used for relatives, friends, time, work, questions, feelings, illnesses, and anything that is not a physical object you carry: nanage obba tamma iddaane, 'to me one younger-brother is' = 'I have a younger brother'; nanage samaya ide, 'I have time'; nanage talenovu ide, 'I have a headache'.

Because the verb agrees with what is possessed: obba tamma iddaane (he is), obbalu akka iddaale (she is), ibbaru makkalu iddaare (they are), ondu prashne ide (it is).

When counting relatives, remember the human number words: obba / obbalu, ibbaru, mooru jana.

guide.title: Things you own or have on you: hattira
guide.text:
Pattern 2 - possessive + ಹತ್ತಿರ (hattira, 'near') + iru. Used for objects and money that you own or have with you: nanna hattira hana ide, 'near me money is' = 'I have money'; avana hattira baik ide, 'he has a motorbike'.

In fast speech hattira is shortened to hatra (ಹತ್ರ): nan hatra hana ide.

The written language also uses ಬಳಿ (bali) in the same way: nanna bali hana ide.

For what a place has, use the locative: namma maneyalli eradu naayi ive, 'in our house there are two dogs' = 'we have two dogs'.

examples.english: We have two dogs at home.

guide.title: Not having, and having in the past
guide.text:
The negative is ಇಲ್ಲ (illa) in place of the form of iru, for every person and number: nanage samaya illa, 'I have no time'; nanna hattira chillare illa, 'I have no change'.

Question: ideyaa? / iddaaraa? - nimma hattira pen ideyaa? 'do you have a pen?'; nimage makkalu iddaaraa? 'do you have children?'. In a question with eshtu the verb is often left out: nimage eshtu makkalu? 'how many children do you have?'

Past: ಇತ್ತು (ittu) for things, ಇದ್ದ (idda) / ಇದ್ಲು (idlu) / ಇದ್ರು (idru) for people; negative ಇರಲಿಲ್ಲ (iralilla). nanna hattira kaaru ittu, 'I had a car'; nanage samaya iralilla, 'I had no time'.

phrases.note: In speech also duddu (ದುಡ್ಡು) for money, and hatra (ಹತ್ರ) for hattira.
Useful with auto drivers and at small shops.
obba = one (male person); the verb is masculine.
obbalu = one (female person); the verb is feminine. Many speakers would use the respectful iddaare for an elder sister.
People also say taim illa (ಟೈಮ್ ಇಲ್ಲ).
tale (head) + novu (pain); the o is long.

phrases.english: We have two dogs at home.
phrases.note: ive is the neuter plural of ide.

phrases.english: How many children do you have?
phrases.note: The verb iddaare can be left out.
Can also mean 'she has no work to do (just now)'.
